data.name: Lawgivers
data.detailed_description:
JUNTE-SE AO NOSSO DISCORD


LAWGIVERS II


Acerca do jogo

Concebido como um mini game com mais de 30.000 cópias vendidas em plataformas móveis, o Lawgivers foi finalmente adaptado para telas de desktop.

Lawgivers

Lawgivers (Legisladores) é um simulador político baseado em turnos. Assuma o controle de um partido e corra para as eleições. Diga aos eleitores o que eles querem ouvir e escolha se deseja cumprir suas promessas ou não. Uma vez dentro do parlamento, aprovar leis importantes e moldar o destino do seu país.

Característicos:


◉ Escolha uma festa, prometa ações aos cidadãos e corra para as eleições
◉ Aprovar ou abolir leis com votos parlamentares
◉ Cuide da experiência, popularidade e lealdade do legislador
◉ Subornar políticos concorrentes para ganhar maioria
◉ Construir relações com outras partes e eleger o presidente

★ 15 nações jogáveis, como os EUA, a Rússia ou o Brasil
★ Mais de 100 leis ordinárias e constitucionais
★ 38 avanços tecnológicos

data.short_description: Lawgivers é um jogo de simulação política baseado em turnos. Corra para as eleições com o seu partido e entre no parlamento para aprovar ou abolir leis. Nomeie o presidente e decida se você quer viver em uma democracia real, ou apenas aparente.

reviews.review:
Lawgivers takes the complicated world of elections, political parties, parliamentary voting, and legislation and transforms it into an approachable turn-based strategy experience. Developed by Damian Bernardi and published by SomniumSoft, the game focuses less on running every detail of a nation and more on the struggle required to obtain and maintain political influence. Elections are only the beginning, as gaining seats in parliament opens the door to proposing laws, negotiating with rival parties, managing politicians, and gradually changing the political direction of the country.

Campaigning establishes the foundation of each playthrough. Your party needs enough public support to gain representation, and promises can be used to attract voters with different priorities. The interesting part is that electoral promises are not simply objectives that must automatically be completed. Players can decide how seriously they intend to honor them once the election is over. This creates an amusing political balancing act between satisfying voters, strengthening the party, and pursuing whatever long-term agenda you have established. It is a relatively simple system mechanically, but it effectively captures the difference between campaigning for power and actually exercising it.

Parliament is where the strategy becomes more engaging. Laws can be proposed, approved, or abolished, but having a political objective does not necessarily mean possessing enough votes to accomplish it. Relationships with other parties therefore become important, particularly when your party lacks a commanding majority. Building cooperation can provide the additional support needed to pass legislation, while less honorable methods such as bribing politicians offer alternative solutions. There is also involvement in presidential appointments, allowing parliamentary influence to extend beyond ordinary legislation.

Individual politicians are more than decorative names attached to parliamentary seats. Experience, popularity, and loyalty influence how useful representatives are to the party, giving players another collection of variables to manage between elections. The character management is intentionally streamlined rather than being a complex social simulation, but it adds enough personality to prevent the political system from feeling completely mechanical. Maintaining a successful party consequently requires attention to internal stability as well as competition with political opponents.

One of the strongest elements is the selection of legislation available. More than 140 ordinary and constitutional laws provide plenty of opportunities to alter the political environment, while dozens of scientific advances can unlock additional events and missions. Constitutional laws are especially interesting because they allow players to influence the underlying rules rather than simply adjusting individual policies. This supports the sandbox nature of the game extremely well. A campaign can begin as a conventional attempt to win democratic elections and eventually evolve into something considerably more ambitious depending on how the player chooses to manipulate the system.

There are 20 playable countries, including major nations such as the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, Russia, and South Korea. These should be viewed as settings for the game's political mechanics rather than perfectly detailed simulations of their real-world institutions. Lawgivers deliberately abstracts many complicated aspects of government so that players can quickly understand what their decisions accomplish. That accessibility makes it easier to experiment with different parties and strategies, although anyone expecting an exhaustive simulation of economics, diplomacy, demographics, bureaucracy, and constitutional procedure may find the experience somewhat simplified.

Visually, the game prioritizes clarity over spectacle. Most of your attention is spent navigating menus, examining political information, monitoring representatives, and making strategic decisions. The modest 2D presentation works reasonably well because elaborate graphics would contribute little to the central gameplay. Hardware requirements are correspondingly lightweight, making the game accessible even on relatively modest computers. Steam achievements and Steam Cloud support provide some additional convenience for players interested in completing multiple campaigns.

Steam Deck compatibility is officially categorized as Playable rather than fully Verified. Performance with the default graphics configuration is considered suitable, and the game can run successfully on SteamOS. However, handheld players should expect compromises. Some functionality is not fully accessible through the default controller configuration, touchscreen interaction or a community controller layout may occasionally be useful, and text entry can require manually opening the virtual keyboard. Some interface text may also appear small, while certain prompts can display keyboard, mouse, or non-Steam Deck controller icons. It is therefore functional on the Deck, but the experience is less seamless than a fully optimized handheld release.

The main limitation is that its accessibility inevitably comes at the expense of simulation depth. Political systems that are enormously complicated in reality are condensed into understandable mechanics, and experienced strategy players may eventually learn how to manipulate those mechanics efficiently. Yet this simplification is also a major reason the game works. It delivers the fantasy of building a political movement, winning elections, forming alliances, controlling parliament, changing legislation, and reshaping a country without burying the player beneath endless administrative detail.

Lawgivers is ultimately an enjoyable political sandbox for players who want strategy centered on elections and parliamentary maneuvering rather than warfare or conventional empire building. Its legislation system, multiple countries, party management, political relationships, and willingness to let players pursue both respectable and questionable routes to power give campaigns considerable personality. It may not be the deepest political simulator available, but its combination of accessibility, freedom, and replayability makes it easy to become absorbed in the pursuit of political influence.

Rating: 8/10
